description: M7 scheduled automation (tasks.md T7.1-T7.3) the serverless way. Add a structured JSON run log emitting the RunReport counts PLUS change counts, wire it into the CLI `run` (which stays the offline equivalent entrypoint), and add a Vercel-Cron `/cron/refresh` web route that runs the pipeline for tomorrow via run_with_snapshot and returns the RunReport+changes as JSON. NO in-process scheduler thread (no APScheduler) — Vercel Cron (declared later in FEAT-005 vercel.json) invokes /cron/refresh daily. Also surface per-event change badges on the index cards. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 (run_with_snapshot, ChangeKind, tally_changes, build_snapshot_store). Independent of FEAT-003 and FEAT-004.
steps: Create vandy_food_radar/pipeline/runlog.py with `run_report_to_json(report: RunReport, changes: dict[str, ChangeKind] | None = None) -> str` returning json.dumps(sort_keys=True) of {target_date (isoformat), fetched, merged, conflicts, cancelled, scored, history_entries, changes: {new,time_changed,venue_changed,cancelled,unchanged}} where the changes object comes from tally_changes(changes) (all zeros when changes is None). Add `log_run_report(report: RunReport, changes: dict[str, ChangeKind] | None = None, *, stream: TextIO = sys.stdout) -> None` printing run_report_to_json to the stream. Type stream as typing.TextIO. Update vandy_food_radar/pipeline/__init__.py to export run_report_to_json, log_run_report.

In vandy_food_radar/cli.py:main, after the existing human-readable print, emit the structured JSON line via log_run_report(report) (the CLI `run`/`seed` still uses the plain print too). Do not change the subcommand surface (seed/run/--db stay). Keep the existing SqliteRepository wiring for the CLI unchanged (CLI is the local/dev path).

In vandy_food_radar/web/app.py, add a `snapshot_store: SnapshotStore | None = None` parameter to create_app and default it to build_snapshot_store(config) when None. Add a route `@app.route('/cron/refresh', methods=['GET','POST'])` that derives Window.from_config(config, today=today_fn()), calls run_with_snapshot(window, repository=repository, sources=_refresh_sources(), location_provider=provider, config=config, snapshot_store=store), and returns a Flask Response with run_report_to_json(report, changes), mimetype 'application/json', status 200.

In vandy_food_radar/web/app.py index view, after building cards, compute per-event change flags by loading the previous snapshot for the target date (snapshot_store.load_snapshot) and calling detect_changes(current_events, previous); attach the ChangeKind for each event's identity_key to its EventCard (add a `change_kind: ChangeKind | None` field to the EventCard dataclass and a human label mapping, e.g. NEW->'New', TIME_CHANGED->'Time changed', VENUE_CHANGED->'Venue changed', CANCELLED->'Cancelled'). Do NOT re-save the snapshot from the index view (read-only); saving happens only in /cron/refresh and /refresh.

In vandy_food_radar/web/templates/_event_card.html render a small change badge when card.change_kind is set and not UNCHANGED, using a state-style span. In vandy_food_radar/web/static/app.css add a `.change-badge` style (reuse the existing state-badge visual language).

In vandy_food_radar/web/wsgi.py build_app(), construct the snapshot store via build_snapshot_store(config) and pass snapshot_store=store into create_app so the deployed app has change-tracking wired (Upstash when env set, in-memory otherwise).

Add tests/test_runlog.py: assert run_report_to_json(RunReport(target_date=date(2025,3,11), fetched=5, merged=4, conflicts=1, cancelled=1, scored=4, history_entries=2), changes) is valid JSON containing target_date and all count keys with the exact values, and a `changes` object whose tallies match a supplied changes dict.

Add tests/test_cron_route.py using create_app over SqliteRepository(':memory:') + InMemorySnapshotStore + today_provider=lambda: date(2025,3,10): POST /cron/refresh returns 200 with mimetype application/json; the JSON parses and contains fetched/merged/scored and a changes object; GET /cron/refresh also works; a second call keeps the target day populated (idempotent) and the snapshot is repopulated. Assert no scheduler thread is created (there is no scheduler symbol to start).
Extend tests/test_web.py minimally: the index page still returns 200 after wiring snapshot_store and change badges, and pre-existing assertions still hold (do not weaken them).
acceptance_criteria: `uv run pytest tests/test_runlog.py tests/test_cron_route.py tests/test_web.py -q` passes.
GET/POST /cron/refresh returns 200 application/json with RunReport counts + a changes object; it runs the pipeline for tomorrow via run_with_snapshot and repopulates the snapshot.
No APScheduler / BackgroundScheduler / in-process scheduler thread exists anywhere; Vercel Cron is the trigger.
CLI `python -m vandy_food_radar run` still works and now also prints a structured JSON run log line in addition to the human-readable summary.
Index cards render a change badge for non-UNCHANGED events; existing web tests still pass unweakened.
`make check` is green (ruff, black --check, mypy strict, pytest); the pre-existing 93 tests still pass.
verification: uv run pytest tests/test_runlog.py tests/test_cron_route.py tests/test_web.py -q
findings: Public symbols FEAT-005 imports: from vandy_food_radar.pipeline import run_report_to_json, log_run_report (in vandy_food_radar/pipeline/runlog.py). run_report_to_json(report: RunReport, changes: dict[str, ChangeKind] | None = None) -> str returns json.dumps(sort_keys=True) of {target_date (isoformat), fetched, merged, conflicts, cancelled, scored, history_entries, changes:{new,time_changed,venue_changed,cancelled,unchanged}}; changes tally comes from tally_changes (all zeros when None). log_run_report(report, changes=None, *, stream: typing.TextIO = sys.stdout) prints that JSON line. /cron/refresh CONTRACT: route registered as @app.route('/cron/refresh', methods=['GET','POST']) in web/app.py; both verbs -> 200 with mimetype 'application/json'; body is run_report_to_json(report, changes) from run_with_snapshot(Window.from_config(config, today=today_fn()), repository, sources=_refresh_sources(), location_provider=provider, config, snapshot_store=store). It runs the pipeline for the target day (tomorrow), reconciles against the previous snapshot, and REPOPULATES the snapshot; a KV outage degrades to all-NEW and never errors. Vercel Cron is the trigger (FEAT-005 declares the schedule in vercel.json) -- there is NO APScheduler/BackgroundScheduler/in-process scheduler symbol anywhere. GOTCHAS: (1) create_app now takes snapshot_store: SnapshotStore | None = None, defaulting to build_snapshot_store(config) when None; web/wsgi.py build_app() constructs the store via build_snapshot_store(config) and injects snapshot_store=store, so the deployed app has change-tracking wired (Upstash when env set, in-memory otherwise). FEAT-005's api/index.py should reuse web.wsgi.build_app (or create_app with the store) so /cron/refresh is available. (2) The index view is READ-ONLY wrt the snapshot: it calls store.load_snapshot + detect_changes to attach per-event change flags but never save_snapshot (saving happens only in /cron/refresh and via run_with_snapshot). (3) EventCard gained change_kind: ChangeKind | None and change_label: str | None; the label is None for UNCHANGED so the template renders a .change-badge span only for NEW/TIME_CHANGED/VENUE_CHANGED/CANCELLED. Label map: NEW->'New', TIME_CHANGED->'Time changed', VENUE_CHANGED->'Venue changed', CANCELLED->'Cancelled'. CSS classes .change-badge / .change-{kind.value} added to web/static/app.css. (4) web/app.py imports flask.Response for the JSON body and aliases werkzeug Response as WerkzeugResponse for the redirect handlers. (5) CLI cli.py:main now calls log_run_report(report) AFTER the existing human-readable print (subcommand surface seed/run/--db unchanged; still uses SqliteRepository). All 123 tests pass (93 pre-existing + 23 FEAT-001 + 7 new: test_runlog.py, test_cron_route.py, +1 test_web.py); make check green (ruff/black/mypy strict/pytest).
